scene.note: A Meter turns each line of the log into events, and watch.js listens: the alarm rings at the first leak, and everything is counted.

steps.note: The meter is fed one line of the log at a time.
For a reading, it emits a reading event with one object of the line's three parts.
Whoever listens gets the object straight away. Blank lines and notes emit nothing.
The meter was made with a limit of litres a minute, and keeps it.
Every reading is emitted as before.
When the litres are more than the limit, a leak event follows, with the same reading.
After a power cut, the logger wrote half a line, and it reaches the meter.
It is not a reading, so the meter emits an error event with an Error that names the line.
With a listener, the error is reported and the next line is read. With none, Node stops the script.
watch.js listens to its meter first, then reads the log a line at a time.
At the first leak the alarm rings, and its listener takes itself off the meter.
Readings and leaks are counted, the later leaks included. Broken lines are reported on standard error.
When the log ends, Imran gets one line with the counts, and the exit code says whether a line was skipped.
